target_customer: Windows music fans who wanted to listen to friends' music libraries
problem: Listeners wanted to play music stored on friends' computers as easily as local files.
business_model: Free desktop client; revenue model not stated

founders.name: Nick Meyer
founders.background_notes: YC lists Kings of Chaos, Reble.FM (Playlist.com), MileWise (Yahoo!), Sup/Wim (Walmart) and Relativity6 without saying which were employers or startups. Later CEO of Provocative. Second founder not named.

competitors.name: Mercora (later Social.FM)
competitors.what: Streamed music from other users' PCs, rebranded Social.FM in 2007

competitors.name: Qloud
competitors.what: Let users share an iTunes library with friends via Facebook
competitors.funding_then: Backed by Steve Case's Revolution LLC

technical_complexity.rationale: A Windows client on the Jabber protocol streaming MP3s between peers needed NAT traversal and client engineering, but was within reach for one coder.

defensibility.rationale: Several similar services existed and the client was easy to copy; it needed friends to install it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Social.FM, a comparable service, shut down by mid 2008; Reble's own end is not documented.

market_need_then: Interest in social music discovery in 2007 and 2008 was high, shown by several competing launches. Legal limits restricted sharing, and Reble streamed only DRM-free MP3s.

branding.domain_note: Used reble.fm, which is now not reachable (HTTP 503 on fetch).
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch covered the public beta launch on 2008-02-05 under a playful headline.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand material survives beyond a single launch article.

outcome_analysis: Reble entered public beta on 5 February 2008 as a Windows only client for streaming friends' music, and is listed by YC as inactive. No shutdown date or cause is public, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned. Comparable services such as Social.FM also closed in 2008, hinting at a hard category, but this is not evidence about Reble itself.
notes: Funding search found no rounds. Outcome search found no shutdown report; the shutdown inference rests only on the YC Inactive status. Site reble.fm returned HTTP 503. Competitor traction data was not sourced. Social.FM shutdown mid 2008 is from a Wikipedia or GigaOM summary in search results.
